Signature Villa, Frond L

A six-bedroom Signature Villa on a Palm Jumeirah frond, held by the same owner since 2007. Not currently for sale. This is the sheet for approaching it.

6 bed 7,000 sq ft built-up 13,000 sq ft plot Gallery View model
Not a live listing

There is no sale instruction, and no asking price exists. The villa does not appear in any sale listing on file. It was marketed to let in February 2025, and the registry shows the same owner since September 2007 with no sale recorded in the Land Department data covering January 2018 to December 2024.

So this is an owner-approach sheet: what the villa is, and what its type has actually transacted at. It is not a brochure to send a buyer, because there is nothing yet to sell.

What the type transacts at

Six- and five-bedroom Signature Villas on the standard plot, sold across the Palm during 2024. These are registered transactions, not asking prices — the distinction the rest of this market blurs.

Land Department transaction register, 2024. Plot approximately 1,245 sq m with 650 sq m built — the same specification as this villa. Frond letters shown; plot numbers deliberately not.

Registered transactions

The type's 2024 range is AED 53M to 61.5M. That is the honest anchor for a conversation with this owner — a recorded price for the same villa type on the same plot size, not a marketing figure.

Read with care

In the source sheet the unit code and the listing link disagree on several rows, so a given price cannot be tied to a given villa with confidence. Treat this as a range, not a row-by-row record. The shape is what matters: Frond L was asking roughly AED 53M to 75M in 2025, against a type that transacted at 53M to 61.5M in 2024.

The rental record

This villa was offered to let in February 2025 at AED 5,000,000 a year, raised within a fortnight to AED 5,500,000, through several agencies at once. Comparable Frond L villas asked AED 6,500,000 to 7,500,000 over the same period.

Whether it let, and at what, is not on file. That is worth knowing before an approach: an owner with a tenant in place and an owner with an empty villa are two different conversations.

Title

Not established

Nobody has read the title deed. Palm Jumeirah is a designated freehold area, but that is a fact about the area, not proof of what this deed says.

Before any tenure statement is made: read the deed, check the Land Department record for mortgages and restrictions, and get the service charge position including any outstanding balance on the plot.

Photography

A photographer has supplied a folder for this villa, shared in September 2026. It is held on the desk record and has not been opened.

No frame is published here. Three checks come first: that the frames show this villa, that no identifiable person appears without their agreement, and that no frame shows the villa number, a gate plate or a neighbour's plate. The last is a publication rule, not a preference.

Before an approach

  • Establish whether it is even available. Nineteen years with one owner, and a rental campaign in 2025, does not read as a seller. Ask before assuming.
  • Find out what happened to the letting. Tenanted or empty changes both the approach and the price.
  • Read the title deed and check the Land Department record for mortgages and restrictions.
  • Get the service charge per square foot, the current year's statement, and any outstanding balance.
  • Confirm the plot and built-up areas against the deed. The 7,000 and 13,000 sq ft figures come from a developer register, not from a survey.
  • Review the photography for subject, for people, and for plates.
